root_cause.text: The SRP initiator's srp_process_rsp() function does not validate that the target-supplied resp_data_len and sense_data_len fields fit within the actual received buffer length, leading to an out-of-bounds read when copying sense data.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that resp_data_len is never checked against the number of bytes actually received (wc->byte_len), and the patch adds a bounds check: `if (sizeof(*rsp) + (u64)resp_len + sense_len <= byte_len)` before performing the `memcpy`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message explicitly states that resp_data_len is never checked against the number of bytes actually received (wc->byte_len), and the patch adds a bounds check: `if (sizeof(*rsp) + (u64)resp_len + sense_len <= byte_len)` before performing the `memcpy`.

candidates.rationale: This condition enables the sense data copy without verifying that the buffer contains valid sense data lengths, allowing an untrusted target to trigger an out-of-bounds read.
This is the start of the memory copy that reads from rsp->data with an offset (resp_data_len) that is not validated against the actual buffer length, directly causing the out-of-bounds read.
This line obtains resp_data_len from the untrusted response without checking if it fits within the buffer, leading to an invalid offset for the sense data copy.
This line uses sense_data_len from the response without validation; if this value is larger than the remaining buffer space, the copy length will be too large and cause an out-of-bounds read.
Although SCSI_SENSE_BUFFERSIZE truncates the copy, the lack of validation of sense_data_len still allows a read from beyond the received buffer when combined with the unchecked offset.
This call site passes the raw received buffer to srp_process_rsp without any length check, enabling the unvalidated fields inside the buffer to cause an out-of-bounds read in the called function.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition gates the sense data copy. Without prior validation of resp_data_len and sense_data_len, an untrusted target can set SRP_RSP_FLAG_SNSVALID to trigger the copy even when the fields are invalid, leading to an out-of-bounds read.
This memcpy uses an offset (resp_data_len) that is taken from the untrusted response without validation. If resp_data_len exceeds the actual buffer length, this reads out-of-bounds.

This is the source offset for the memcpy, derived directly from the target-supplied response. Since there is no check that resp_data_len is within the received buffer, this allows an attacker to specify an arbitrary offset, causing an out-of-bounds read.

This determines the copy length using sense_data_len from the response. Without validation, an attacker can set a large sense_data_len that, combined with the unchecked offset, causes the copy to read beyond the allocated buffer.

Although SCSI_SENSE_BUFFERSIZE caps the copy to the destination buffer, it does not prevent an out-of-bounds read from the source if the offset or length would extend past the received response buffer.

This call site passes the raw received buffer to srp_process_rsp without any length or field validation. This allows the attacker-controlled resp_data_len and sense_data_len fields inside the buffer to be processed without bounds checking, enabling the out-of-bounds read.
